transcript.en: In my presentation, I'm going to talk about coffee, and its importance both in economic and social terms.
transcript.zh: 在我的报告中，我将谈论咖啡，以及它在经济和社会方面的重要性。

transcript.en: We think it was first drunk in the Arab world, but there's hardly any documentary evidence of it before the 1500s,
transcript.zh: 我们认为这最早是在阿拉伯世界被饮用，但在十六世纪之前几乎没有任何文件证据，

transcript.en: although of course that doesn't mean that people didn't know about it before then.
transcript.zh: 当然这并不意味着人们在此之前不知道咖啡。

transcript.en: However, there is evidence that coffee was originally gathered from bushes growing wild in Ethiopia, in the northeast of Africa.
transcript.zh: 然而，有证据表明，咖啡最初是从非洲东北部的埃塞俄比亚野生灌木丛中采集的。

transcript.en: In the early sixteenth century, it was being bought by traders,
transcript.zh: 在十六世纪初期，它被商人买下，

transcript.en: and gradually its use as a drink spread throughout the Middle East.
transcript.zh: 并逐渐在整个中东地区用作饮料。

transcript.en: It's also known that in 1522, in the Turkish city of Constantinople, which was the centre of the Ottoman Empire,
transcript.zh: 我们也知道，1522年，在土耳其的奥斯曼帝国中心君士坦丁堡市，

transcript.en: the court physician approved its use as a medicine.
transcript.zh: 法院医生批准将其用作药物。

transcript.en: By the mid-1500s, coffee bushes were being cultivated in the Yemen
transcript.zh: 到了十六世纪中叶，也门正开始种植咖啡灌木丛，

transcript.en: and for the next hundred years this region produced most of the coffee drunk in Africa and the Arab world.
transcript.zh: 并且在接下来的一百年里，这个地区生产了非洲和阿拉伯世界的大部分咖啡。

transcript.en: What's particularly interesting about coffee is its effect on social life.
transcript.zh: 咖啡最有趣的地方是它对社会生活的影响。

transcript.en: It was rarely drunk at home, but instead people went to coffee houses to drink it.
transcript.zh: 人们很少在家里喝咖啡，而是要去咖啡厅喝

transcript.en: These people, usually men, would meet to drink coffee and chat about issues of the day.
transcript.zh: 这些人，通常是男人，会聚一聚喝咖啡，聊天谈论当天的事情。

transcript.en: But at the time, this chance to share ideas and opinions was seen as something that was potentially dangerous,
transcript.zh: 但是在那个时候，分享想法和意见的机会被认为是一种潜在的危险，1

transcript.en: and in 1623 the ruler of Constantinople demanded the destruction of all the coffee houses in the city,
transcript.zh: 1623年君士坦丁堡的统治者要求摧毁所有的咖啡厅。

transcript.en: although after his death many new ones opened, and coffee consumption continued.
transcript.zh: 在这个城市，尽管在他死后，开设了许多新的咖啡厅，咖啡的消费也在继续。

transcript.en: In the seventeenth century, coffee drinking spread to Europe, and here too coffee shops became places where ordinary people, nearly always men, could meet to exchange ideas.
transcript.zh: 在十七世纪，喝咖啡流传到欧洲，在这里咖啡也变成了普通人，几乎所有男人都可以见面交流思想的地方。

transcript.en: Because of this, some people said that these places performed a similar function to universities.
transcript.zh: 正因为如此，有人说咖啡厅与大学有类似的功能。

transcript.en: The opportunity they provided for people to meet together outside their own homes and to discuss the topics of the day had an enormous impact on social life,
transcript.zh: 他们为人们在家外聚会并讨论当天的主题提供了机会，对社会生活产生了巨大的影响，

transcript.en: and many social movements and political developments had their origins in coffee house discussions.
transcript.zh: 许多社会运动和政治发展起源于咖啡厅的讨论。

transcript.en: In the late 1600s, the Yemeni monopoly on coffee production broke down and coffee production started to spread around the world, helped by European colonisation.
transcript.zh: 在17世纪后期，也门对咖啡生产的垄断被打破，咖啡生产开始在世界各地传播，这得益于欧洲殖民化。

transcript.en: Europeans set up coffee plantations in Indonesia and the Caribbean and production of coffee in the colonies skyrocketed.
transcript.zh: 欧洲人在印度尼西亚和加勒比地区建立了咖啡种植园，而殖民地的咖啡产量也猛增。

transcript.en: Different types of coffee were produced in different areas, and it's interesting that the names given to these different types,
transcript.zh: 不同类型的咖啡产于不同的地区，有趣的是，这些不同类型的名称，

transcript.en: like Mocha or Java coffee, were often taken from the port they were shipped to Europe from.
transcript.zh: 如摩卡咖啡或爪哇咖啡，通常是从他们从他们被装运的港口取得的。

transcript.en: But if you look at the labour system in the different colonies, there were some significant differences.
transcript.zh: 但是如果你看看不同殖民地的劳动制度，就会有一些显著的差异。

transcript.en: In Brazil and the various Caribbean colonies, coffee was grown in huge plantations and the workers there were almost all slaves.
transcript.zh: 在巴西和加勒比各个殖民地，咖啡种植在大片种植园里，那里的工人几乎都是奴隶。

transcript.en: But this wasn't the same in all colonies: for example in Java, which had been colonised by the Dutch,
transcript.zh: 但是，在所有的殖民地中，这一点并不一样：例如在荷兰殖民的爪哇，

transcript.en: the peasants grew coffee and passed a proportion of this on to the Dutch, so it was used as a means of taxation.
transcript.zh: 农民种咖啡，并将其中一部分给了荷兰人，所以它被用作税收手段。

transcript.en: But whatever system was used, under the European powers of the eighteenth century, coffee production was very closely linked to colonisation.
transcript.zh: 但无论采用何种制度，在十八世纪的欧洲列强下，咖啡生产与殖民化密切相关。

transcript.en: Coffee was grown in ever-increasing quantities to satisfy the growing demand from Europe,
transcript.zh: 为了满足欧洲日益增长的需求，

transcript.en: and it became nearly as important as sugar production, which was grown under very similar conditions.
transcript.zh: 咖啡的种植量不断增加，而它的重要性几乎与在类似条件下种植的糖一样重要。

transcript.en: However coffee prices were not yet low enough for people to drink it regularly at home, so most coffee consumption still took place in public coffee houses and it still remained something of a luxury item.
transcript.zh: 然而，咖啡价格还不足以让人们在家里定期饮用咖啡，所以大多数咖啡消费仍然发生在公共咖啡厅，并且仍然是一种奢侈品。

transcript.en: In Britain, however, a new drink was introduced from China, and started to become popular,
transcript.zh: 然而，在英国，从中国引进了一款新的饮料，并开始流行起来，

transcript.en: gradually taking over from coffee, although at first it was so expensive that only the upper classes could afford it.
transcript.zh: 逐渐取代咖啡，尽管一开始它太贵了，只有上层阶级才能喝得起。

transcript.en: This was tea, and by the late 1700s it was being widely drunk.
transcript.zh: 这就是茶。到1700年代末，大部分地区都开始了喝茶。

transcript.en: However when the USA gained independence from Britain in 1776, they identified this drink with Britain,
transcript.zh: 然而，当美国在1776年从英国获得独立时，他们将这种饮料与英国联系在一起，

transcript.en: and coffee remained the preferred drink in the USA, as it still is today.
transcript.zh: 咖啡仍然是美国的首选饮料，就像今天一样。

transcript.en: So, by the early nineteenth century, coffee was already being widely produced and consumed.
transcript.zh: 所以，到十九世纪初，咖啡已经被广泛生产和消费。

transcript.en: But during this century, production boomed and coffee prices started to fall.
transcript.zh: 但在本世纪，咖啡产量猛增，咖啡价格开始下跌。

transcript.en: This was partly because new types of transportation had been developed which were cheaper and more efficient.
transcript.zh: 这在一定程度上是因为开发了更便宜，更高效的新型运输方式。

transcript.en: So now, working people could afford to buy coffee - it wasn't just a drink for the middle classes.
transcript.zh: 所以现在，工人们可以买得起咖啡了 - 它已经不仅仅是中产阶级的饮料了。

transcript.en: And this was at a time when large parts of Europe were starting to work in industries.
transcript.zh: 而此时正值欧洲大部分地区开始工业领域制造的时候。

transcript.en: And sometimes this meant their work didn't stop when it got dark:
transcript.zh: 有时候，这意味着他们的工作在天黑时还没有完成：

transcript.en: they might have to continue throughout the night.
transcript.zh: 他们可能不得不整夜继续工作。

transcript.en: So, the use of coffee as a stimulant became important —
transcript.zh: 所以，使用咖啡作为兴奋剂变得很重要 -

transcript.en: it wasn't just a drink people drank in the morning, for breakfast.
transcript.zh: 不仅仅是人们早上喝的早餐。

transcript.en: There were also changes in cultivation ...
transcript.zh: 种植方面也发生了变化……
